facts.claim: Skill level is not a damage parameter of any cast. constructAbilityObject has no level argument; levelUpAbility only increments the SkillTreeData level byte (cap 0x14=20); the level only raises the point cap (getMaxPoints = level + additionalMaxPointsFromStats).
evidence: dump/decomp/LE.dll/AbilityObjectConstructor.c: constructAbilityObject(Ability, Vector3, Vector3, UseType, GameObject, Boolean, Boolean, AbilityMutator, Boolean, AbilityInfo, Single, AbilityID, Boolean, Vector3)

facts.claim: What a cast uses instead of a level: (1) the AbilityMutator registered for the cast Ability in the caster's AbilityMutatorManager when the constructAbilityObject mutator argument is null; if none exists the bare Ability asset is the AbilityInfo; (2) levelScaling x CharacterData.Level (character level) and attributeScaling x attribute, only if constructor.applyScalingStats (+0x88) is set (levelScaling additionally needs a CharacterDataTracker, i.e. the player); (3) the constructor's Stats (+temp stats) snapshot.

facts.claim: abilityGrantedByNode (basis of category nodeGranted: 189 abilities, 805 nodes) is a UI tooltip hint, not a cast mechanism: SkillTreeNode.abilityGrantedByNode@0x110 is read only by NodeTooltipManager/SkillsPanelManager to open a UITooltipAbility beside the node tooltip. The real grant is in <Skill>Tree.updateMutator (fields written into a Mutator) and in the mutator/prefab/CharacterMutator code that casts.

facts.claim: Casts made by CharacterMutator (passives, pp-indexed uniques/affixes/idols, hard-coded) call constructAbilityObject on the PLAYER's own constructor (CharacterMutator.aoc@0x20C0) with mutator=null, AbilityInfo=null and UseType 0 (Indirect). They get: player global stats, ApplyConditionalTemporaryStats/ApplyRelevantCooldownStats for the CAST ability's tags, the cast ability's own registered mutator (if any), and AbilityProperty fields keyed by the cast ability ID. They do NOT pass through the mutator or temp stats of any bar skill. constructAbilityObject itself charges no mana and no cooldown (Ignivar Head note 'free cast'); some paths charge explicitly (CastFrostClaw: BaseMana.reduceMana(cost*0.8)).
evidence: CharacterMutator.c OnFirstMeleeHit (~25965, Fire Aura on melee): RngElement_Roll(); ProcTimeTracker_TryProc(*(param_1+0xc00)); constructAbilityObject(lVar16 [aoc],uVar14 [Ability 0xa2],...)
UseType.cs: Indirect=0, Direct=1, InstantDirect=2, DelayedCast=3, SummonerCast=4, Echo=5, Shadow=6, ... (a triggered cast is not 'direct')

facts.claim: Sub-abilities cast by an ability object (ChanceToCastOnHit/Kill/WhenHit, CastAfterDuration, CreateAbilityObjectOn*): the object's own AbilityObjectConstructor (GetOrAdd on the object, or the creator's constructor when useCreatorConstructor=true) calls constructAbilityObject with mutator=null. An object's constructor has no AbilityMutatorManager (GetComponent on the object) so mutator stays null; each created object copies the constructor's Stats.stats list (with the temp stats added for this cast) into its own Stats. So a sub-ability inherits the stats snapshot of the owner's cast (owner tree temp stats included) unless useCreatorConstructor routes it through the player constructor (then S1 applies). Per-prefab values (castChance, cooldownDuration, castPTT, useCreatorConstructor) are serialized prefab data not in the extracted JSON.
evidence: ChanceToCastOnHit.cs: ability@0x88 castChance@0x90 useCreatorConstructor@0x95 cooldownDuration@0xA0 requiresMelee/Crit/Kill/RareOrBoss/Player castPTT@0xE0 limitCasts minimumHitsPerTargetBeforeCast

facts.claim: ProcTimeTracker(limit, interval) allows at most `limit` procs in any sliding `interval` seconds (array of the last `limit` proc times; TryProc succeeds when some slot time+interval < now and overwrites it). In chance-to-cast code the chance Roll happens before TryProc, so a failed roll does not consume a slot: rate = min(events*min(1,chance), limit/interval).
evidence: ProcTimeTracker.c TryProc: if (fVar1 + fVar2 < fVar7) { slot[i] = Time.time; return 1 }
RngElement.Roll(p): p<=0 false, p>=1 true (research/06b section 2.2)

facts.claim: Damage tags of a granted/triggered cast are owned by the cast ability's own damage component, not by the trigger source: buildDamageStatsForHolder(holder, stats) = buildDamageStats(holder.baseDamageStats, holder.damageTags(+0x98), stats...). tags: isHit ? (tags & ~DoT)|Hit : (tags & ~Hit)|DoT; type bits are added from base damage > 0. AbilityInfo.getTags (ability/mutator tags; FireAuraMutator.getTags converts Fire to Cold/Lightning) govern conditional/extraTag stat checks. Fire Aura: damage[Fire]=14, damageTags=Spell|DoT (4352), isHit=0, ADE 0.7, attributeScaling[attribute 2 = Intelligence in the client order]: +4% increased all damage, +1 added Spell damage, +4% prop 67 per point. Spell/Fire/DoT-tagged player stats apply; Hit/Melee-tagged stats do not (the melee attack that triggers Flame Walker lends nothing).
evidence: abilities.json FireAura damage[0]: damageByType {Fire:14}, damageTagNames [Spell,DoT], addedDamageScaling 0.7, isHit 0, attributeScaling [{attribute 2, stats: [inc 0.04 tags 0; added 1.0 tags 256; prop67 inc 0.04]}]

facts.claim: A granted ability that has a registered mutator is configured by ANY source that writes that mutator, independent of who casts it: Flame Ward's tree writes FireAuraMutator.{increasedDamageFromFlameWard, increasedDurationFromFlameWard, coldConversionFromFlameWard, lightningConversionFromFlameWard}; passives write FireAuraMutator.{increasedDamageFromPassives, increasedAreaFromPassives, manaPerFireAuraOnHighCostMelee, coldConversionFromPassives, lightningConversionFromPassives, staticChargesOnFireAura}; items/idols write AbilityStatsMutatorManager fields keyed by ability ID (FireAura #0 increasedFireAuraDamage@0x758 read by FireAuraMutator.getIncreasedDamage; #3 fireAuraBaseDamagePerSecond; #5 fireAuraMoreDamagePerRes@0x814 read in getTempStats). Tree writes happen only for specialised skills (updateMutator runs for each loaded SkillTreeData). 48 mutator classes are written by two or more trees (cross_tree_mutator_writes / skill_node_effects.mutators).
evidence: LocalTreeData.c loadSkillTree (~10671: updateMutator for each loaded tree) and updateMutator (switch on AbilityID -> <Skill>Tree.updateMutator)
skill_node_effects.json tree 'Flame Ward' mutators [BurstOfFlameMutator, FireAuraMutator, FlameWardMutator]

facts.claim: Granted-only abilities (categories nodeGranted/sub/abilityIdOnly) have no skill tree of their own (skillTree is 'treeID:nodeID' = the granting node). A cast ability that is also a specialisable player skill (Frost Claw, Smite, Upheaval, Glacier, Static Orb, Meteor, Lightning Blast, Maelstrom, Elemental Nova, Vengeance, Rip Blood ...) uses the SAME mutator as its bar version, so its tree applies iff that skill is specialised on a slot.
evidence: cm_code_casts.json: 26 'player' category abilities cast by hard-coded CharacterMutator paths

facts.claim: Basic attack: bar slot index 4 of the default bar [skill, null, null, null, BasicPlayerAttack, Evade] holds ba1 (BasicPlayerAttack, AbilityID 95). PlayerAbilityList.setAbility swaps it for ability.+0x208 (BasicPlayerBowAttack, AbilityID 624) by Ability.abilityReplacementWeaponCondition (+0x204): 1=Bow -> when WeaponInfoHolder.usingBow, 2=NotBow -> when not bow, 3=Always (the value stored on ba1 is not in the extracted data: UNKNOWN; the Bow-variant relation is FACT). Damage record: DamageEnemyOnHit base Physical 2.0, isHit 1, crit 5%/x2, addedDamageScaling 1.0 (full added/weapon damage), tags Physical|Melee (bow: Physical|Bow). Speed: speedScaler AttackSpeed, useDuration 0.75, mana 0; AttackSpeed gets the weapon attackRate multiplier iff (bow equipped ? tag Bow : tag Melee); dual wield averages the two rates.

classes.json basicAttackReplacer (Primalist Swipe, Mage Mana Strike, Sentinel Rive, Acolyte Harvest, Rogue Puncture) is NOT a combat mechanic: when the class unlocks that skill (ExperienceTracker level-up) and bar slot 4 still holds ba1 (AbilityID 95) or the bow attack (624), the new skill is auto-equipped into slot 4 and Notifications.NewSkill(ability, replaceBasicAttack) is shown. One-time auto-equip.
evidence: ExperienceTracker.c ~890-944: lVar10 = *(longlong *)(lVar10 + 0xb0) (CharacterClass.basicAttackReplacer) compared with the new ability; slot 4 compared with Ability_getAbility(0x5f) / Ability_getAbility(0x270); then Notifications_NewSkill(uVar12,cVar5)

facts.claim: The basic attack is also a trigger source: CharacterMutator.OnFirstMeleeHit(Ability, Actor, ...) fires for any melee ability including ba1 (Fire Aura via Flame Walker/Burning Hands, Frost Claw, Lightning Blast, Volcanic Orb ...). Mastery/class abilities are ordinary equippable skills: CharacterClass.knownAbilities / unlockableAbilities / Mastery.masteryAbility feed KnownAbilityList.calculateAbilityList; nothing casts them automatically.

Transform forms (Werebear, Spriggan, Swarmblade, Reaper; isTransform=1) replace the bar while transformed: PlayerAbilityList.SetTransformAbilities / ReplaceTransformAbility / SemiTransform and AbilityManager.transformSkills (list of {transformAbilityID, abilities}); the FormChanger prefab lists the form bar (transformAbilityList[]), customEvadeAbility, transformBackAbility, transformReplacementSkill (Reap). Form skills share the player skill's playerAbilityID/tree where IDs coincide (WerebearSwipe1 sw43 = Swipe tree, which writes WerebearSwipeMutator). Exact per-form bar composition beyond the FormChanger references = UNKNOWN.
